matches.rationale: GT 1 describes inflated performance claims in the abstract (2×–50×) that are not uniformly supported by experimental data. Pred 3 identifies that Figure 1's caption claims '50x improvements' but Table 1 shows the maximum is actually 600x and minimum is 1.7x. Pred 4 notes Section 4.2 claims 'over 50x gains' but only one of three humanoid tasks exceeds 50x. Both findings capture the same issue of overstated/inconsistent performance claims.

GT 2 describes confusion about how depth is defined (total Dense layers vs. discrete levels 4, 8, 16, etc.) and inconsistency between architecture description and experiment reporting. None of the findings address this definitional inconsistency about what constitutes 'depth' in the paper.

GT 3 concerns undisclosed modifications to training regimes, learning rates, or compute budgets for very deep networks (up to 1024 layers), limiting reproducibility. None of the findings identify missing protocol details or training regime disclosures for extreme depths.

GT 4 describes overstated claims about qualitatively distinct emergent behaviors at certain depths (Section 4.3), with limited evidence from humanoid visualizations. Pred 6 identifies that Figure 6 data shows anomalous collapse at depth 16, conflicting with Section 4.3's claim that depth 16 is critical for the Humanoid agent learning to walk upright. Both address the same issue of unsupported claims about depth-dependent behavioral changes.
GT 5 identifies a fabricated reference (Neumann and Gros, 2022) on multi-agent RL scaling laws. None of the findings mention this or any other fabricated/unverifiable citation.

GT 6 concerns omission of limitations discussion regarding compute requirements and environmental impact in the Conclusion. None of the findings identify missing ethical or limitations content about computational costs or accessibility.

GT 7 describes inflated rhetorical language in the abstract ('unlock substantial improvements,' 'significantly boost performance'). None of the findings specifically identify overly promotional or inflated language as a rhetorical issue.

GT 8 describes modified numbers in Figure 6 showing consistently higher performance when both actor and critic are scaled jointly, but actual ablations reveal cases where individual scaling outperforms joint scaling. Pred 6 identifies anomalous data patterns in Figure 6 where critic-depth-16 shows systematic collapse inconsistent with the scaling narrative, suggesting possible data integrity issues in the same figure.

GT 9 describes Section 4.5 claiming batch size scaling becomes effective with large depth (citing Figure 7), but the figure shows inconsistent/minimal improvements. Pred 2 identifies the exact same contradiction: the caption/title claim batch size scaling is unlocked by depth, but the body text states 'only marginal or inconsistent improvements' and 'the overall benefit...remains uncertain.'

GT 10 concerns missing ethical considerations in the Conclusion/Impact Statement regarding carbon footprint, reproducibility challenges, and societal implications. None of the findings identify omitted ethical content or impact statement deficiencies.

GT 11 describes overly promotional language in the Introduction ('unlocks the ability to scale,' 'surpass those from scaling width alone'). None of the findings specifically address rhetorical overstatement in the Introduction.

GT 12 identifies unrealistically large performance improvements (983× on Humanoid Big Maze) in Table 1 that inflate impact. Pred 3 identifies that Table 1 reports Humanoid Big Maze improving 600× (0.06 → 40), which the caption understates as '50x improvements.' Both findings address inflated/inconsistent performance numbers in Table 1 for Humanoid Big Maze, though the exact multipliers differ slightly.

GT 13 describes inconsistency between defining critic output as L2 distance in Preliminaries but later using dot-product similarity in experiments. None of the findings identify this methodological inconsistency in the critic network definition.

GT 14 concerns undisclosed environment version discrepancies (MJX/Brax) in Appendix B.2 that affect reproducibility. None of the findings mention environment version issues or physics simulation discrepancies.

GT 15 describes overstated claims that CRL is critical for depth scaling, while alternate methods (GCBC, GCSL) show mixed benefits. None of the findings address the generalizability claims about CRL versus other methods.

GT 16 identifies inconsistent wall-clock time scaling in tables for depths beyond 64 layers, with unusually low times for extremely deep models. Pred 7 identifies that Tables 3 and 4 report conflicting wall-clock times for the same environment (Humanoid U-Maze), differing by ~2.7×, and that Table 4's depth 128-1024 entries double exactly (suspicious). Both address data integrity issues in wall-clock time reporting.

GT 17 describes overgeneralized claims in the conclusion about deep models exhibiting qualitatively better behaviors based on limited humanoid visualizations. While Pred 6 mentions Section 4.3's claims about depth 16 being critical, it focuses on data anomalies rather than the broader overgeneralization of qualitative behavior claims in the conclusion.
